sources.scope: Unit namespace path-view mechanisms relevant to a read-only `/`: ProtectSystem= values, ReadOnlyPaths=, BindReadOnlyPaths=, TemporaryFileSystem= and the RootDirectory=/RootImage= root views
sources.anchor: § RootDirectory=, § RootImage= and § BindPaths=/BindReadOnlyPaths= (PATHS); § ProtectSystem=, § ReadWritePaths=/ReadOnlyPaths= and § TemporaryFileSystem= (SANDBOXING); systemd 262.1 man-page footer; page opened 2026-10-20
sources.teaches: Among ProtectSystem= values, `full` mounts `/usr/`, `/boot`, `/efi` and `/etc/` read-only but does not cover `/`, while `strict` mounts the entire hierarchy read-only except `/dev/`, `/proc/` and `/sys/`, with `ReadWritePaths=`, `StateDirectory=`/`LogsDirectory=` and the `PrivateTmp=` `/tmp` caveat as documented exceptions; `BindReadOnlyPaths=` creates read-only bind mounts and `TemporaryFileSystem=` accepts the `ro` mount option, so a read-only unit view of `/` is not exclusive to strict or `ReadOnlyPaths=`; the `RootDirectory=`/`RootImage=` sections present root path views without stating that they make the root read-only, and the page establishes no host's active configuration
